findings.question: does verification admit the guarded form and reject the unguarded one?
can the library hold a concept that raises on its own domain?
does requiring totality lose the generalising reach the concept bought?

not_claimed: totality is checked on a probe grid, not proved -- a concept can raise at a point the grid does not contain

the counter-risk is real: a legitimately useful partial concept (e.g. a guarded reciprocal that callers promise never to feed zero) is now rejected, and this benchmark cannot show that because it only contains candidates I chose
rejection is by domain, not by call-site contract; there is no way to say 'total on the inputs this program will actually use'
